customer_question: Before we approve the Review Page for Submission, are there any issues with how the Model Number, product description text, or Publish Date fields are filled in?
question_variants: Should the Model Number field include the full product name or just the model code?
Does our product description's Bluetooth version claim need to match our actual registration?
How does the Product Publish Date field actually get set?
actual_issue: Before Submission, three Review Page content issues needed to be caught and addressed: whether the Model Number field should contain the full descriptive product name or just the core model code, whether a stated Bluetooth version in the product's marketing description text matched the registration's actual Core spec version, and confusion over how the Product Publish Date field is determined.
plain_english_explanation: A few small but important details on the final review screen before a registration is filed are easy to get wrong: putting a long descriptive name where a short model code is expected, leaving an old Bluetooth version number in marketing text after the actual registration was updated to a newer version, and not realizing that the publish date field isn't something you set directly -- it just reflects whenever the registration actually gets filed.
consultant_answer: (1) The registration confirmation document listed the Model Number as a full descriptive name ('Explosion proof hands free unit [model code]'), but the conventional practice is to use just the model code portion as the Model Number, which is what was entered. (2) The product's simple English description text stated 'compliant with Bluetooth V4.1,' but this registration was for v5.2 -- since this was still correctable, the customer was asked whether to update it, and they confirmed it should be corrected to v5.2. (3) The Product Publish Date field showing a specific date was explained as simply reflecting whatever date Submission is actually executed (for example, submitting the next day would show that next day's date) -- it is not a field set independently in advance, and the customer confirmed they were fine with whatever the earliest possible date turned out to be.
decision_logic: Before Submission, the Review Page should be checked for: the Model Number field reflecting the conventional core model code rather than a longer descriptive name; any Bluetooth-version claim in product description text matching the registration's actual Core spec version; and the Product Publish Date field being understood as a reflection of the actual Submission date rather than an independently configurable field.
final_recommendation: When reviewing a Review Page before Submission, check the Model Number field uses the conventional core model code, confirm any Bluetooth-version claim in product description text matches the registration's actual Core spec version and correct it if not, and clarify to the customer that the Product Publish Date field simply reflects the actual Submission date rather than needing separate configuration.
risk_if_done_wrong: Leaving a full descriptive name in the Model Number field, an outdated Bluetooth-version claim in product description text, or misunderstanding the Publish Date field as independently configurable could each create an inaccurate or confusing public-facing registration record.
